Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 33 s. 2023 MAY 2023 HON. EDWIN JUBAHIB Governor, Davao del Norte Dear Gov. Jubahib: This has reference to your letter dated November 14, 2022 requesting for guidance on whether road infraStructure projects fall under Peace and Order Program under DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2022-118 or the "GUIDELINES ON THE DEVELOPMENT AND FORMULATION OF THE PEACE AND ORDER AND PUBLIC SAFETY PLAN (POPS-PLAN) 2023-2025. Per your submission, road infrastructure projects such as road openings, road rehabilitation and road maintenance address the underlying cause of conflict in fragile and conflict-affected communities. Roads are driver of long-term economic growth, peace and resilience as it enables access to basic services and economic opportunities for all. Simply put — where the road ends, insurgency begins. Hence, your request for guidance on the matter. At the outset, your attention is invited to Section 4 of the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-143 or the Omnibus Guidelines for Peace and Order Councils (POCs) dated August 27, 2019 where the terms "Peace and Order Program" (POP), "Peace and Order and Public Safety (POPS) Plan", and 'Public Safety Programs" were defined, to wit: 4.10. Peace and Order Programs (POP) includes projects, programs, and activities (PPAs) that directly address criminality, armed conflict, and human right violations and bring about the achievement of justice, peace and order. It can also be any or combination of PPAs enumerated in Section 3.23 of JMC No. 2015-01, dated January 9, 2015. Xxxx 4.13 Public Safety Programs (PSP) covers activities that protect the community from dangers threateninq their qeneral welfare and safety, and address the focus areas of: (i) road and vehicle safetv, (ii) jail management and (iii) emergency/crisis management and fire safety. (Emphasis ours) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Peace and Order Programs directly addresses criminality, armed conflict and human right. These programs were enumerated and defined in DILG MC No. 2022-118 dated 19 September 2022, particularly, Item 4.4.2.1, viz: 4.4.2.1 PEACE AND ORDER PROGRAM 4.4.2.1.1 Crime and disorder — violations of the law and situations that disrupts harmonious living within a community. . . . . —Illegal drugs — a mandatory sub-area, in compliance to Republic Act No. 4.42111 9165 or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act Of 2022. xxx 4.4.2.1.2 Conflict — Refers to a situation where two or more groups are in the disagreement with each other or in disagreement with the State. The source of disagreement may be the control and possession of resources, when one party feels deprived, offended or oppressed by another or by the policies and programs of the State. 4.4.2.1.2. I Violent extremism and terrorism 4.4.2. I .2.2 Insurgency/armed conflict 4.4.2.1.2.3 Prevalence of private armed groups, contributing to the proliferation of gun culture, "rido" or clan wars, unjust use of military and police auxiliaries 4.4.2.1.3 Threats to the environment and human security (illegal logging, illegal mining, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUUF), smuggling, illegal activites related to quarrying, etc.) xxx On the other hand, Public Safety Programs are enumerated in Item 4.4.2.2, thus: 4.4.2.2 PUBLIC SAFETY PROGRAM 4.4.2.2.1 Road and vehicle safety concerns 4.4.2.2.2 Emergency/crisis management and fire safety concerns 4.4.2.2.3 Establishment and maintenance of CCTVs 4.4.2.2.4 Unregulated use of firecrackers 4.4.2.2.5 Other public safety concerns that may be deemed necessary In view thereof, road infrastructure projects do not fall under the Peace and Order Program as the same do not directly address criminality, armed conflict, and human right violations. Assuming arguendo that your point of view is true — that road openings, road rehabilitation and road maintenance addresses the underlying cause of conflict in fragile and conflict-affected communities, to our mind, it does not directly addresses criminality, armed conflict, and human right violations, rather, road infrastructure projects are a consequence of addressing such insurgencies. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. Page 2 of 3

We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY T RITY OF THES RETARY: ATTY N VI OR R.
